finding.claim: The purge handler performs a destructive purgeAll() without enforcing the admin permission. checkPerm's result is discarded, so any user who reaches the route, including one without admin, can trigger the purge.
finding.source: Any request reaching the purge route; user loaded from request context via userFrom (handlers.go:25, 40). The user's Perms are not checked.

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) loads the user from context

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14) returns a bool but is never enforced. mustPerm (handlers.go:16-22) is not called here, though rotateKeys (handlers.go:33) uses it correctly. No auth middleware or route registration exists in the directory, so upstream enforcement could not be verified.

verdict.guard_found: In-handler: checkPerm at handlers.go:12-14 returns a bool, but its result is discarded at handlers.go:26, so it is not an effective guard. mustPerm (handlers.go:16-22) exists but is not called in purge(); rotateKeys (handlers.go:33) uses it correctly. No route registration or upstream auth middleware appears in the directory (Grep for Route/Handle found none).
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: checkPerm(u, "admin") at handlers.go:26 has its bool discarded, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any user, but whether a non-admin can reach purge() depends on routing or middleware (not in the directory), so the attacker tier cannot be determined from the code available.

finding.claim: userFrom uses an unchecked single-value type assertion, so a request whose context lacks the userKey value panics. net/http recovers the panic per request, so this is a low-severity availability and log-noise issue, not a bypass.
finding.source: A request whose context has no userKey value, e.g. a route not wrapped by auth middleware.

trace.note: type assertion panics when the context value is missing

finding.guards_checked: None in userFrom. The panic occurs before purgeAll or rotateAll runs, so the failure is fail-closed. A nil *User would also panic in checkPerm or mustPerm, which is likewise fail-closed.

verdict.guard_found: No guard inside userFrom. Between the request and the assertion at handlers.go:40, the only control is none: purge (handlers.go:25) calls userFrom directly. rotateKeys (handlers.go:32-33) calls userFrom first, so the panic happens before mustPerm at line 33. The only userKey setter in the directory is none; grep finds userKey only at lines 40 and 42, so nothing in this code sets the context value.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: userFrom at handlers.go:40 does an unchecked single-value assertion, so a request without a *User under userKey{} panics, as the candidate says. The candidate's conclusion that this is "not a bypass" is incomplete, because purge at handlers.go:26 discards the bool from checkPerm, so purge has no effective admin check and any request that does carry a user reaches purgeAll() at line 27, a real authorization bypass the candidate missed.
